<!--

Add a mutex to the downloading of playback files from a reolink camera.
Some Reolink cameras dont handle it well if mutiple files are downloaded simultaniously, besides it will not be faster to download in parralel vs sequentially since you are limited by the SD card speed and ethernet speed anyways.

If two playbacks are opend at the same time, one will start downloading emidiately (spinning icon in the UI with the playback bar filling up to fully grey), the other will wait (spinning icon) untill the first one finishes and then starts downloading (spinning icon with playback bar filling up).

@edenhaus I am not entirely sure if I like this PR or not.
It is a attempt to fix https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/137167, but that seems to be specific to the iOS app which seems strange in itself. (it apears the iOS app requests 2x the playback stream simultaniously).

However it does slow down playing recordings on my Home Hub since you need to first wait for the first download to finish before starting the next download.

In testing on my own system, simultanious downloads on my Home Hub were no problem and made the whole playback experiance more snappy in the GUI withouth this lock.

I dont have any iOS devices, so I am unable to test or reproduce.

I think before continuing with the PR, we should have someone reproduce this.
Becuase it is now based on a single user and having the mutex will slow down things quite a bit.

This PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/141015 seems to be heading in a much better direction.

Therefore I will close this.

I think it's how the files are served - Safari appears to insist on [proper content-range handling](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/AppleApplications/Reference/SafariWebContent/CreatingVideoforSafarioniPhone/CreatingVideoforSafarioniPhone.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40006514-SW6). review_comments:
Why aren't you using:

```python
lock = asyncio.Lock()

# ... later
async with lock:
    # access shared state
```

I know it's equivalent to try/finally, but I prefer the above over it as you don't need to manually release the lock in the finally block.

I agree that I also like `async with lock:` a lot more, however in this particular case it is not possible to use that.

This is because within the `async with lock:` I do a retry of the same function which would again enter a `async with lock:` block wich will cause a dead-lock.....

Therefore before doing the retry I need to mannually release the lock.
And then in the finnaly I need to check if the lock is already released, because the retry will already release the lock in its finally block after which you go up 1 in the callstack and then enter the same finnaly block again. this time the lock is already released.

See also comment below.
Why are you realising the lock here manually?

Because if you don't release the lock here, the next call `await self.get(.....` which is a retry of this whole function will get stuck in a dead-lock since it will try to do `await self._download_mutex.acquire()` while it is already acquired (one function up in the callstack, which was the first try).

Can we create a new function where we use the lock? So we could handle the exception and call the new function in this function so we don't have the recursive call.
I don't like to manually handle the acquiring/releasing of locks as it could lead to errors. For example, in the future, we have another use case where we need to recursively call this function. In this case, the dev needs to know that he needs to manually release the lock first, which is weird, imo.
